subject: Re: [EXTERNAL] - [Thank You] Encord AI Leaders Dinner
text:
Hi Skander,
Sorry for taking so long to respond, these last few weeks have been a bit busy. Thank you for inviting us, the conversations and food were great.

I'll have to take a look at that book. Relatedly, a paper from neuroscience that has made its way into ML is Rao and Ballard (1999) https://www.cs.utexas.edu/~dana/Rao.pdf. When I was in neuroscience, my research was related, and examined how the dynamics of the local networks in the input layer to the cortex (layer 4) affected information processing, which is still something I think about.

Predictive coding is most prevalent in ML with variational methods (e.g., learning factor graphs) as well as residual networks (there's a nice paper by Schmidhuber that covers why residual networks might not be doing what we think they are).

I should have time to talk next week if you'd like. I've discussed potential integration points with Oscar, and I think there are some interesting places we may be able to use your software, but right now we're heads down in trying to put together the basic pipelines.

Thank you,

subject: RE: [External] Data for Monday's Demo
text:
Dear Jennifer,

We primarily use the “MHD” file format for our image outputs (FAIRsharing | MHA/MHD<https://fairsharing.org/FAIRsharing.hrttzm>), which results in two files per image, the “raw” for image data and “zraw” for label data.
The “zraw” file requires the metadata information in the corresponding “mhd” file because it is compressed, and the decompression info is in the mhd data.
You can view the .mhd contents in any text editor, it’s all stored as plain text inside, including the information about the image dimensions.
If the current Encord tools aren’t able to support MHD file formats yet, please let us know and we can figure another option out.

All the best,
Ivan

For your records reference, here is an overview of our Audio Data Annotation Workflow:
1. Preprocessing Raw Audio Files:
• Convert audio codec to PCM-16 (cle) for compatibility, Change file format to .wav and set the sampling rate to 8kHz.
• This step follows the standard process from the 937 use-case and is performed locally.
2. Uploading and Assignment:
• Processed files are uploaded to the annotation tool.
• The project manager assigns the files to annotators.
3. Human Transcription:
• Annotators transcribe the audio based on shared guidelines.
• Once completed, files are marked as “Transcription Complete.”
4. Quality Review:
• Dedicated quality checkers review all completed transcriptions.
• Files that pass the review are marked as “Passed QA.”
5. Random Inspection:
• The project manager conducts random checks on files
